map.目标层深反推保温时间：已知目标层深（如 0.8 mm）时由 δ = k√t 反推: Back-calculate holding time from target depth: given a target depth (e.g. 0.8 mm), invert delta = ksqrt(t) to find the needed holding time, avoiding over-holding that coarsens grains and wastes energy.
map.温度—时间权衡：提高温度可缩短渗碳时间，但同时加大变形与晶粒长大风险，用层深系数: Temperature-time trade-off: raising temperature shortens carburizing time but increases distortion and grain-growth risk; the case-depth factor k quantifies temperature's effect on depth (for 850-950 C).
map.算例：渗碳温度 930 ℃、保温时间 6 h: Example: carburizing temperature 930 C, holding time 6 h
map.层深系数 k = 0.42 + (930 − 900) × 0.0016 = 0: Case-depth factor k = 0.42 + (930 - 900) x 0.0016 = 0.468; total depth delta = 0.468 x sqrt(6) = 1.146 mm; effective hardened depth (550HV1) ~ 0.75delta = 0.860 mm; holding time to reach 0.8 mm total depth = (0.8 / 0.468)^2 = 2.92 h; average carburizing rate = 1.146 / 6 = 0.1911 mm/h.
map.渗碳层深为什么随时间: Why does carburized depth grow with time
map.渗碳是碳原子在奥氏体中的扩散控制过程，扩散层深度与 √t 成正比（抛物线规律）。: Carburizing is a diffusion-controlled process of carbon atoms in austenite; the diffusion-layer depth is proportional to sqrt(t) (parabolic law). Thus a 4x increase in holding time only doubles the depth, and efficiency diminishes with time.
map.低于 850 ℃ 时碳扩散速度过慢、渗碳效率极低；高于 950 ℃ 晶粒急剧粗化: Below 850 C carbon diffusion is too slow and carburizing efficiency is very low; above 950 C grains coarsen sharply and distortion grows. Outside this range use another process or staged carburizing; this tool warns on out-of-range input.
map.这是根据该温度区间的渗碳层深数据拟合出的层深系数经验式（温度每升高 10 ℃，k: This is an empirical case-depth factor fitted from carburizing-depth data in this temperature range (k rises about 0.016 per 10 C). In production use your own calibrated G value and carburizing atmosphere carbon potential; the fitted formula is only for order-of-magnitude estimation.
map.有效硬化层深为什么取 75%？: Why take effective hardened depth as 75%?
map.550HV1 界限硬度对应的深度一般出现在总层深的 70%–80%，取 0.75: The depth at the 550HV1 limit hardness is generally 70%-80% of total depth; 0.75 is taken as the median estimate. Hardenability, quenching method and cooling rate vary greatly by material; for critical parts use the measured hardness-gradient curve.
